doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: The book, discography and the internet
summary: His book will include a discography of 1200-2000 records, assembled with Ed Dennis; he comments on errors on the internet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: In your book, you said you’re working on a book, will it have a discography?
Yeah. We’re going to have — I’d say we’re probably going to have anywhere from twelve hundred to two thousand.
Records and sessions, different records. We should have at least that. What the young man is doing now, Ed Dennis, I mean I have about four or five hundred that I’ve always had.

Yeah. LPs. Oh man he’s — 45s — LPs that I’ve totally forgot. One time LPs with people. I mean it’s just ridiculous. It’s absolutely ridiculous that I just didn’t remember. And then when I heard this — oh I know this, oh this was so-and-so. I mean all of a sudden it just came back to me or who’s it was and who’s date it was. And that’s what happened during the course of him finding records that he’s found from other people that he’s been doing on the internet.

Well the Internet is a good thing but the internet can also be a bad thing. Because there is a lot of stuff that’s on the internet that didn’t happen. And people are taking credit for a lot of stuff that they didn’t do. Because somebody went out and did some work and started writing some information and they thought that this was what was going on. They
didn’t do all their homework. But yet they’re making a fortune behind putting somebody else’s name on it. And some of that is also now being corrected.
